Role: Risk / Compliance / RM
Preconditions: Approved exception exists with reason, amount, validity, review date and supervisor decision.
Test data: Approved underinsurance exception on an underinsured collateral.
Steps:
1. Approve the exception.
2. Open coverage dashboard.
3. Open exception register.
4. Run monitoring before expiry.
5. Resolve the exception and run monitoring again.
Expected: The approved exception remains visible in compliance/exception reporting until it is resolved or expires; it is not hidden or treated as proof that the underlying coverage ratio is adequate.

Ref: BR-06; BR-03; BR-11; US-06.3; US-11.1; ITMD Response 2 | ITMD Response 2
Scenario: Coverage formula traceability — Primary and aggregate-exposure inputs are identifiable in coverage assessment
Preconditions:
Role: Risk / Compliance
Preconditions: Building collateral has land and structure values and is secured to multiple facilities; approved coverage formula has been signed off.
Test data: Structure value, land value, active insured amount, facility balances and configured coverage percentage.
Steps:
1. Open the coverage calculation details.
2. Verify the primary Bank-assessed insurable input excludes land.
3. Verify aggregate outstanding exposure across all linked facilities is available as a secondary test.
4. Inspect formula version/configuration and output.
Expected: The calculation exposes the approved primary insurable-value input and aggregate linked-facility exposure input. Final numeric expected amount must follow the signed-off interpretation recorded in the Clarifications sheet.
Notes: Dependency: Blocked pending business resolution of the difference between Clarification Log's max(outstanding, collateral value) statement and ITMD's primary-plus-secondary test description.

Ref: BR-09; BR-10; US-09.3; US-10.1; Business Clarification Log | Business Clarification Log
Scenario: Customer notification cap — Customer receives no more than one notification per day
Preconditions:
Role: Customer
Preconditions: Customer has multiple policies/items due on the same calendar day.
Test data: Two or more due customer reminders on one day.
Steps:
1. Prepare multiple due reminders for one customer.
2. Run the notification job.
3. Inspect outbound customer notifications for that day.
4. Run the job again.
Expected: No more than one customer notification is sent to the same customer per day. Multiple due items are consolidated or otherwise handled within this daily cap; repeated job runs do not duplicate delivery.

Ref: BR-09; BR-10; US-09.3; US-09.6; US-10.2; Business Clarification Log | Business Clarification Log
Scenario: Collateral substitution — Customer reminders stop when collateral is substituted or policy is otherwise resolved
Preconditions:
Role: RM / RO
Preconditions: Expired or expiring policy is being monitored; an approved collateral substitution/resolution is recorded.
Test data: Policy/collateral linkage before and after substitution.
Steps:
1. Run reminders while the policy is unresolved.
2. Complete approved collateral substitution/resolution.
3. Run reminder job again.
4. Inspect policy and notification history.
Expected: Customer reminders stop once the policy is renewed or collateral is substituted/otherwise resolved, and the resolution is retained in history.

Ref: BR-07; BR-18; US-07.1; US-07.2; US-07.3; US-18.2; Business Clarification Log | Business Clarification Log
Scenario: Branch/corporate-center routing — Branch/Corporate Center maker and checker routing follows clarified role mapping
Preconditions:
Role: RO / Corporate RO / RM / BM / Corporate RM
Preconditions: Branch and Corporate Center workflow configurations have been established from the clarification response.
Test data: Branch maker RO or Corporate RO; checker RM/Branch Manager/Corporate Center Manager/Corporate RM as applicable.
Steps:
1. Submit a Branch transaction as RO.
2. Verify routing to the configured RM/Branch Manager.
3. Submit a Corporate Center transaction as Corporate RO.
4. Verify routing to the configured Corporate Center Manager/Corporate RM.
5. Verify maker-checker separation.
Expected: Transactions route to the applicable configured checker for their organizational context; no generic checker receives all transactions.

Ref: BR-07; BR-18; US-07.1; US-07.2; US-07.3; Business Clarification Log | Business Clarification Log
Scenario: Corporate sector routing — Corporate sector transaction routes from Relationship Officer to Corporate Relationship Manager
Preconditions:
Role: Corporate Relationship Officer / Corporate Relationship Manager
Preconditions: Corporate sector workflow mapping is configured.
Test data: Corporate RO maker and Corporate RM checker.
Steps:
1. Log in as Corporate Relationship Officer.
2. Submit a policy transaction.
3. Open Corporate Relationship Manager inbox.
4. Verify the task is assigned within the correct scope.
5. Attempt self-approval as maker.
Expected: Corporate sector transaction routes to the Corporate Relationship Manager checker; maker cannot approve the same transaction.

Ref: BR-07; BR-12; BR-18; US-07.4; US-12.1; Business Clarification Log | Business Clarification Log
Scenario: Exception workflow evidence — Selecting Exception exposes evidence upload and retains normal workflow routing
Preconditions:
Role: RO / designated checker / supervisor
Preconditions: Policy submission form supports the exception checkbox and normal workflow.
Test data: Exception reason and supporting evidence document.
Steps:
1. Start the relevant policy transaction.
2. Select the Exception checkbox.
3. Verify the supporting-document upload field appears.
4. Attach evidence and submit.
5. Verify normal workflow routing and supervisor approval path.
Expected: Exception selection exposes the supporting-evidence upload, retains the document reference and routes through the normal configured workflow with required supervisor approval.

Ref: BR-08; BR-15; US-08.4; US-15.2 | User Story Format V1
Scenario: Secure preview/download — Document preview and download enforce authorization and record download history
Preconditions:
Role: Authorized user / unauthorized user / Auditor
Preconditions: A confidential document is linked to a customer/collateral and roles with different scopes exist.
Test data: Document ID and users within/outside its authorized scope.
Steps:
1. Preview and download as authorized user.
2. Inspect download history.
3. Attempt preview/download as unauthorized user using direct API/document reference.
4. Inspect denial audit.
Expected: Authorized users can preview/download according to assigned permissions and data scope; unauthorized users are denied even with a guessed document ID. Download history is recorded.

Ref: BR-08; US-08.7 | User Story Format V1
Scenario: Advanced document search — Document search supports all specified search dimensions
Preconditions:
Role: RO / Documentation Officer
Preconditions: Test repository contains documents with distinct customer, CIF, facility, collateral, policy, title deed, registration, segment, region, district, branch, type, status, expiry and upload-date values.
Test data: Each specified search key, individually and in supported combinations.
Steps:
1. Search by customer name and CIF.
2. Search by loan reference, collateral ID and policy number.
3. Search by title deed and registration number.
4. Search by segment, region, district and branch.
5. Search by document type, status, expiry date and upload date.
Expected: Search returns matching documents for each specified filter and respects the user's authorized data scope.

Ref: BR-08; US-08.8 | User Story Format V1
Scenario: Archive management — Archived documents remain retrievable and cannot be deleted without authorization
Preconditions:
Role: Documentation Manager / Auditor
Preconditions: Document archive feature and Bank-approved records retention policy are configured.
Test data: Active, archived and retention-restricted documents.
Steps:
1. Archive an eligible document.
2. Retrieve it through authorized search.
3. Attempt unauthorized deletion.
4. Verify retention and audit details.
Expected: Documents can be archived and retrieved according to the configured retention policy; unauthorized deletion is prevented and archive actions are audited.
Notes: Dependency: Requires Bank records-retention policy and archive configuration; no retention duration is assumed.

Ref: BR-08; US-08.1; US-08.2 | User Story Format V1
Scenario: Multi-entity association — Documents can be associated with the applicable customer, loan, collateral and policy
Preconditions:
Role: RO / Documentation Officer
Preconditions: Customer, facility, collateral and policy records exist.
Test data: Document references for a policy certificate, loan agreement, title deed and collateral release.
Steps:
1. Upload each document type.
2. Associate each document with the correct business entity.
3. Retrieve each document from its entity view.
4. Verify unrelated records do not receive the association.
Expected: Documents are linked to the correct customer, loan, collateral or insurance policy; associations are retained and do not leak to unrelated records.

Ref: BR-13; US-13.1 | User Story Format V1
Scenario: Executive dashboard completeness — Executive dashboard displays the complete BRD-defined KPI set
Preconditions:
Role: Senior Manager
Preconditions: Representative data exist for insured/uninsured collateral, expiring/due-soon/expired policies, renewals, compliance, insurer exposure, exceptions, aging and workload.
Test data: Controlled data set covering every KPI category.
Steps:
1. Log in as an authorized Senior Manager.
2. Open executive dashboard.
3. Verify each of the 11 specified dashboard measures.
4. Reconcile displayed values to underlying records.
Expected: Dashboard displays Total Insured Collateral, Uninsured Collateral, Policies Expiring within 30 Days, Policies Due within 7 Days, Expired Policies, Renewals in Progress, Compliance Status, Insurance Company Exposure, Exception Summary, Policy Ageing and Operational Workload. Values reconcile to source data.

Ref: BR-13; US-13.2; BR-16; US-16.2 | Code-gap review
Scenario: Scheduled report artifact — Scheduled report produces an actual PDF/Excel artifact, not only a notification
Preconditions:
Role: Report scheduler / authorized recipient
Preconditions: A report schedule and definition exist; output format is selected; test storage/delivery provider is configured.
Test data: Scheduled report with defined filters and PDF or Excel format.
Steps:
1. Create/enable a schedule.
2. Set the report due for execution.
3. Run the scheduler.
4. Verify report data retrieval and generated file.
5. Inspect generation and delivery status separately.
Expected: A real report artifact is generated with the scheduled definition and filters. A 'generated' notification without an artifact is a failure. Delivery status is distinct from generation status; simulator delivery is labeled simulated.
Notes: Dependency: Local artifact generation can be tested in development; live email/DMS delivery requires provider integration.

Ref: BR-13; US-13.2 | User Story Format V1
Scenario: Ad-hoc reports and trends — Ad-hoc reporting supports filtering, trend analysis and drill-down
Preconditions:
Role: Authorized report user
Preconditions: Historical policy and collateral data across multiple periods and organizational scopes are available.
Test data: Date period, segment, branch, policy status and insurer filters.
Steps:
1. Run an ad-hoc report for a selected period.
2. Apply segment/branch/status filters.
3. Inspect trend analysis across periods.
4. Drill down to underlying policy/collateral records.
5. Verify data scope.
Expected: Report output reflects selected filters and period, supports trends and drill-down, and does not expose records outside the user's authorized scope.

Scenario: Audit event completeness — Audit trail records login, document, workflow, exception and notification events
Preconditions:
Role: Internal Auditor
Preconditions: Audit logging is enabled; authorized auditor is available.
Test data: Login/logout, approval, document upload/version, exception update, notification and configuration change.
Steps:
1. Execute each listed activity.
2. Open audit history.
3. Verify actor, timestamp, action, previous/new values where applicable and reference.
4. Attempt modification/deletion as business user.
Expected: Audit trail captures the BRD/US-defined activity categories; business users cannot edit/delete audit records; retention follows Bank policy.

Ref: BR-14; BR-15; US-14.1; US-15.2 | Code-gap review
Scenario: Access-scope audit query — Audit search/export does not disclose records beyond the user's permission
Preconditions:
Role: Auditor / ordinary business user
Preconditions: Audit records exist across multiple branches/segments and role permissions are configured.
Test data: Audit records for own scope and outside scope.
Steps:
1. Query audit records as ordinary business user.
2. Attempt to query another branch/segment by changing filters.
3. Query as authorized Auditor.
4. Compare returned records with role scope.
Expected: Audit endpoints enforce role and scope on the backend; read-only Auditor access follows the configured authorized scope. Direct API calls cannot retrieve unauthorized audit records.

Ref: BR-16; US-16.2; US-13.2 | User Story Format V1
Scenario: Reporting/BI integration — Reporting/BI integration exports approved reporting data securely
Preconditions:
Role: System / BI consumer
Preconditions: BI integration endpoint and authentication are approved and configured.
Test data: Approved report dataset and consumer identity.
Steps:
1. Request/export an authorized report dataset.
2. Authenticate the BI consumer.
3. Verify data fields and organizational scope.
4. Simulate endpoint failure.
5. Inspect logging and retry.
Expected: Authorized reporting data is exchanged through the approved secure integration; errors are logged and retry/monitoring status is visible. No BI integration is claimed if not configured.
Notes: Dependency: Live test requires BI endpoint, interface contract and service identity.

Ref: BR-16; US-16.1; US-02.6 | User Story Format V1
Scenario: CBS loan closure/facility changes — CBS facility closure and changes synchronize without duplicating records
Preconditions:
Role: System / CBS integration
Preconditions: CBS test adapter contains customer and facility already synchronized to CBAIMS.
Test data: Loan closure, product/facility amendment and changed outstanding amount.
Steps:
1. Amend facility data in CBS test source.
2. Run sync.
3. Verify CBAIMS facility update.
4. Close the facility in CBS source.
5. Run sync again.
6. Verify linkage and audit/history.
Expected: Customer/facility changes and loan closure are reflected in CBAIMS; duplicate facilities are not created; existing collateral links/history are reconciled.

Ref: BR-16; US-16.3; US-04.7 | User Story Format V1
Scenario: Government registry verification — Government ownership/registration verification is reported only when authoritative source responds
Preconditions:
Role: RO / authorized verifier
Preconditions: Government registry connector is configured and authorized access is available, or simulator mode is explicitly identified.
Test data: Property registration/ownership reference and registry response.
Steps:
1. Submit a verification request.
2. Inspect source and response reference.
3. Test positive, negative and unavailable responses.
4. Compare recorded verification status with actual response.
Expected: Where integration is available, ownership, registration status and ownership changes are verified from the authoritative source. Where unavailable, status remains manual/pending and is not falsely marked externally verified.
Notes: Dependency: Live verification requires government authority endpoint, agreement and credentials; BR-16 says 'where available'.

Ref: BR-16; US-16.4 | User Story Format V1
Scenario: Integration retry and monitoring — Integration failures are logged, monitored and retried without duplicate business processing
Preconditions:
Role: System Administrator / Integration Operator
Preconditions: At least one integration is configured with observable retry/monitoring behavior.
Test data: Transient timeout, authentication failure, malformed response and repeated retry.
Steps:
1. Trigger a transient provider timeout.
2. Inspect failed/pending integration record.
3. Restore provider and retry.
4. Repeat a request to check idempotency.
5. Inspect integration audit.
Expected: Failures and retries are visible with timestamps and error categories. Successful retry is recorded; repeated delivery does not create duplicate customer/facility/document transactions. No unsupported retry interval is assumed.

Ref: BR-04; US-04.7; US-14.1 | User Story Format V1
Scenario: Ownership verification audit — Ownership verification records actual verifier and verification date
Preconditions:
Role: Authorized verifier
Preconditions: Ownership record is pending verification; authorized verifier has valid session.
Test data: Owner details, verification result, remarks and evidence.
Steps:
1. Attempt verification as unauthorized role.
2. Verify rejection.
3. Log in as authorized verifier.
4. Complete verification with remarks.
5. Reopen the record and audit history.
Expected: Only authorized user can verify; actual authenticated user and timestamp are recorded; request-supplied user IDs cannot set verifier identity.

Ref: BR-04; US-02.4; US-04.4 | User Story Format V1
Scenario: Ownership percentage storage — Joint-owner identities and individual percentages are retained
Preconditions:
Role: RO
Preconditions: Collateral is jointly owned and owner identities are validated.
Test data: Two or more owners with individual percentage entries.
Steps:
1. Capture each legal owner and applicable identity fields.
2. Enter each ownership percentage.
3. Save and reopen the record.
4. Verify audit and displayed values.
Expected: Each owner's identity and entered percentage are retained. Any total-share validation is applied only if the Bank confirms a specific rule.

Ref: BR-05; BR-06; US-05.1; US-06.10 | User Story Format V1
Scenario: Multiple policies under one customer — Multiple distinct policies can be linked to one unique customer ID
Preconditions:
Role: RO
Preconditions: Customer exists with a unique CIF and more than one valid insurance policy.
Test data: Two distinct policy numbers for one customer.
Steps:
1. Register the first policy.
2. Register a second distinct policy for the same CIF.
3. Open the customer profile.
4. Verify both policies and unique identities.
Expected: Multiple valid policies are associated with one unique customer ID. A policy can only be linked once to the same customer; legitimate multiple policies are not blocked.

Ref: BR-06; US-06.4 | User Story Format V1
Scenario: Expired policy rejection — Expired policy cannot be accepted as a current insurance policy
Preconditions:
Role: RO
Preconditions: Policy registration is open and collateral requires insurance.
Test data: Effective/expiry dates where expiry is before current system date.
Steps:
1. Enter an already-expired policy period.
2. Submit policy registration.
3. Inspect validation and workflow state.
Expected: Expired policy is rejected for current registration/activation; it cannot satisfy current insurance coverage.

Ref: BR-09; US-09.5; US-09.7 | User Story Format V1
Scenario: Renewal completion monitoring — Renewal status, completion date, responsible officer and turnaround time are tracked
Preconditions:
Role: RM / Branch Manager
Preconditions: Renewal workflow exists with responsible officer assignment and timestamps.
Test data: Renewal submitted, approved and completed at known timestamps.
Steps:
1. Submit a renewal.
2. Record maker/responsible officer.
3. Approve renewal.
4. Open renewal monitoring/report.
5. Verify status, completion date and turnaround calculation.
Expected: Renewal monitoring displays renewal status, completion date, responsible officer and turnaround time, using stored event timestamps.

Ref: BR-12; US-12.1; US-12.2 | User Story Format V1
Scenario: Exception identification and assignment — Insurance exceptions are identified, assigned and investigated
Preconditions:
Role: RO / RM / Risk
Preconditions: Test records include expired policy, underinsurance, missing insurance, missing documents, unapproved insurer, renewal delay and policy inconsistency.
Test data: One record for each documented exception category.
Steps:
1. Trigger each exception condition.
2. Verify exception creation/alert.
3. Assign responsible user.
4. Add investigation note/evidence.
5. Review exception history.
Expected: Each documented exception category is identified, assigned, alerted and tracked with investigation history.

Ref: BR-12; US-12.3; US-12.4 | User Story Format V1
Scenario: Corrective action and closure — Exception closure records corrective action and resolution date
Preconditions:
Role: Assigned officer / supervisor
Preconditions: An open exception is assigned and supporting evidence is available.
Test data: Corrective action, resolution evidence and completion date.
Steps:
1. Open assigned exception.
2. Record corrective action.
3. Attach resolution evidence where applicable.
4. Submit for closure/review.
5. Inspect status and history.
Expected: Exception status changes only through the authorized workflow; corrective action, evidence and completion date are retained.

Ref: BR-13; US-13.1; US-13.2 | User Story Format V1
Scenario: Policy aging and workload reports — Policy aging and operational workload measures reconcile to underlying records
Preconditions:
Role: Authorized manager
Preconditions: Dataset includes policies of different ages/statuses and operational task assignments.
Test data: Policies with different effective/expiry dates; pending/overdue workflow items.
Steps:
1. Generate policy-aging view/report.
2. Generate operational-workload view/report.
3. Inspect underlying policy/task records.
4. Reconcile totals and grouping.
Expected: Policy aging and operational workload are presented using actual recorded policy/task data and authorized scope; no hardcoded demo values are used.

Ref: BR-17; US-17.6; US-17.8 | User Story Format V1
Scenario: Encryption in transit — Sensitive browser/API communication uses Bank-approved TLS
Preconditions:
Role: Security tester
Preconditions: Production-like TLS endpoint, certificate chain and approved protocol baseline are available.
Test data: Application URL and protected API requests.
Steps:
1. Connect to the application over the production-like endpoint.
2. Inspect negotiated TLS protocol/cipher and certificate chain.
3. Attempt insecure HTTP access.
4. Inspect redirection/denial behavior.
Expected: Sensitive application traffic is encrypted using Bank-approved secure protocols; invalid certificates and prohibited insecure transport are not silently accepted.
Notes: Dependency: Requires infrastructure evidence and Bank-approved TLS baseline.

Ref: BR-17; US-17.6 | User Story Format V1
Scenario: Encryption at rest/key protection — Sensitive stored data and encryption keys meet Bank-approved at-rest controls
Preconditions:
Role: Security / Infrastructure
Preconditions: Database, backup and document-storage encryption configuration and key-management evidence are available.
Test data: Database storage, backup, sensitive document storage and key-management configuration.
Steps:
1. Inspect DB/storage encryption configuration.
2. Inspect backup encryption evidence.
3. Inspect key storage/access controls.
4. Verify keys are not stored with encrypted data or exposed in source/logs.
5. Record infrastructure evidence.
Expected: Sensitive data at rest and backups follow Bank-approved encryption standards; keys are protected under enterprise key-management controls. Application-level password hashing is not mistaken for full storage encryption.
Notes: Dependency: Requires infrastructure/KMS evidence; cannot be proven solely from application UI.

Ref: BR-11; BR-08; US-11.4; US-08.5 | User Story Format V1
Scenario: Ownership document monitoring — Missing and expired ownership documents are identified in monitoring
Preconditions:
Role: RM / Documentation Officer
Preconditions: Portfolio contains collateral with valid, missing and expired ownership documents.
Test data: Title deed, vehicle registration, machinery certificate and other applicable mandatory documents.
Steps:
1. Open ownership-document monitoring.
2. Filter for missing documents.
3. Filter for expired documents.
4. Drill down to affected collateral.
5. Verify status and document history.
Expected: Monitoring identifies missing and expired ownership documentation and links each issue to the correct collateral/document requirement.

Ref: BR-11; US-11.3; US-06.5 | User Story Format V1
Scenario: Duplicate insurance monitoring — Duplicate insurance monitoring identifies duplicates without rejecting legitimate distinct policies
Preconditions:
Role: RM / Risk
Preconditions: Policy dataset contains one true duplicate and two distinct policies for a shared customer/collateral.
Test data: Policy number, customer ID, collateral reference and insurer combinations.
Steps:
1. Create/identify a duplicate policy record using the same documented policy identity.
2. Run duplicate monitoring.
3. Review the alert.
4. Compare with distinct legitimate policy records.
Expected: True duplicate insurance records are identified using the policy/customer/collateral/insurer identity attributes. Distinct legitimate policies are not falsely merged or rejected.

Ref: BR-06; BR-11; US-06.9; US-11.1 | User Story Format V1
Scenario: Insured amount capture — Insured amount is captured as a positive monetary value and audited
Preconditions:
Role: RO
Preconditions: Policy registration is open for collateral requiring insurance.
Test data: Positive insured amount; zero; negative amount; amended amount.
Steps:
1. Enter a positive insured amount and submit.
2. Verify it is stored with the policy/collateral valuation details.
3. Attempt zero and negative values.
4. Amend insured amount through the authorized policy lifecycle.
Expected: Only a positive insured amount is accepted; authorized additions/updates are reflected in the relevant record and audit log with user/date/time.

Ref: BR-11; BR-13; US-11.6; US-13.1; US-13.2 | User Story Format V1
Scenario: Branch/RM compliance reporting — Branch-wise and RM-wise compliance reports respect organizational scope
Preconditions:
Role: Branch Manager / RM
Preconditions: Test portfolio spans multiple branches and relationship managers.
Test data: Branch and RM filters with insured, uninsured, expiring and exception records.
Steps:
1. Generate branch-wise compliance report.
2. Generate RM-wise compliance report.
3. Reconcile underlying policies/collateral.
4. Attempt to request an unauthorized branch.
Expected: Reports provide branch-wise and RM-wise compliance views and reject unauthorized scope requests.

Ref: BR-12; US-12.4 | User Story Format V1
Scenario: Exception escalation history — Unresolved exceptions are escalated according to configured SLA and history is retained
Preconditions:
Role: Department/District Business Director
Preconditions: Exception escalation SLA and recipient mapping are approved/configured.
Test data: Open exception beyond configured SLA.
Steps:
1. Create and assign an exception.
2. Advance test date beyond its configured SLA.
3. Run exception monitoring.
4. Inspect escalation recipients and history.
Expected: Unresolved exceptions are escalated according to the approved configured SLA; escalation history is retained. No numeric SLA is invented.
Notes: Dependency: Requires approved exception SLA and role/recipient mapping.
